basic_information.official_title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A LEVEL II DISTRICT HOSPITAL WITH ONE HUNDRED (100) BED CAPACITY IN THE MUNICIPALITY OF MAIMBUNG, PROVINCE OF SULU, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
signed_by: Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after publication in a newspaper of regional circulation

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Creates a new 100-bed Level II district hospital in Maimbung, Sulu, run under the Integrated Provincial Health Office of Sulu rather than directly by the regional Ministry of Health.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: To bring Level II hospital services into Maimbung, and into Sulu's provincial health network, rather than leaving residents dependent on facilities further away.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: A hospital that did not exist is established in law, with 100 beds at Level II. Its chief must submit an annual operational plan, and any future expansion must follow an annual hospital development plan.
who_will_be_affected: Residents of Maimbung and nearby municipalities in Sulu
Patients currently travelling for Level II services
The Integrated Provincial Health Office – Sulu, which supervises it
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: In force since 2022. The hospital's existence in law does not by itself mean it is built.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. A 100-bed Level II district hospital is established in Maimbung, Sulu — supervised by the provincial health office, with its funding carried in the annual regional budget.
in_practice: A Level II district hospital with 100-bed capacity in Maimbung
Under the direct administrative and technical supervision of the Integrated Provincial Health Office – Sulu
Salaries and operating costs come through the annual General Appropriations Act of the Bangsamoro
The hospital chief submits an annual operational plan to the regional Ministry of Health
Future expansion follows an annual hospital development plan

for_specific_groups.Patients in Sulu: Level II services in Maimbung rather than a journey to a provincial or regional facility.
for_specific_groups.The provincial health office: IPHO-Sulu holds direct administrative and technical supervision — unusual among these acts, most of which report to the regional ministry.
for_specific_groups.Hospital management: An annual operational plan covering programmes, projects, activities and budget must go to MOH-BARMM.

what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: In force since 2022; delivery depends on annual appropriations.
what_you_can_do: Ask IPHO-Sulu about the hospital's status and its annual hospital development plan
Ask what the annual operational plan submitted to MOH-BARMM contains
watch_out_for: The act names no peso amount and sets no construction deadline.
It creates the hospital in law; whether it has been built is a separate question the text does not answer.
Unlike the upgrading acts, this one has no implementing-rules clause and no Universal Health Care integration clause.

key_terms_explained.Level II hospital: A facility with specialist departments beyond basic emergency and general medicine.
key_terms_explained.IPHO: Integrated Provincial Health Office — the provincial body running local health facilities.
key_terms_explained.RLED: The Regulation and Licensing Enforcement Division of the regional health ministry, which sets the operational guidelines for the facility.
key_terms_explained.PS / MOOE: Personnel Services (salaries) and Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses (running costs).

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Dhu Al-Qa'dah 17, 1443 / 16 June 2022, approved by the Chief Minister on 12 July 2022.

where_to_complain.oversight: Integrated Provincial Health Office – Sulu, which has direct administrative and technical supervision; and MOH-BARMM, which receives the annual operational plan

everyday_scenarios: A resident of Maimbung needing Level II care previously travelled to a larger facility. This act establishes one in the municipality.
Someone wanting to know whether the hospital will expand can ask for the annual hospital development plan — Section 1 makes any future increase in bed capacity depend on it.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Establishes a Level II District Hospital with 100-bed capacity in the Municipality of Maimbung, Province of Sulu, under the direct administrative and technical supervision of the Integrated Provincial Health Office – Sulu. Any future increase in bed capacity and upgrading of health care services and facilities must be based on the annual hospital development plan prepared by the hospital administration in coordination with IPHO-Sulu.

Section 2 — MOH-BARMM, specifically the Regulation and Licensing Enforcement Division, shall immediately include in the Ministry's programme the operational guidelines of a Level II facility with 100-bed capacity in accordance with national Department of Health standards.
Section 3 — Funding for Personnel Services and Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses shall be included in the annual General Appropriations Act of the Bangsamoro.

Section 4 — The Chief of Maimbung District Hospital, in consultation and coordination with IPHO-Sulu, shall submit to MOH-BARMM an annual operational plan reflecting the programmes, projects, activities and budgetary needs for the hospital's operation.
Section 7 — Takes effect 15 days after publication in a newspaper of regional circulation.

related_legislation.related_note: Part of the June 2022 cluster of hospital acts. Unlike the upgrading acts in that cluster, it places the facility under the provincial health office rather than the regional ministry.

implementation_status.irr_status: None required by the act; the RLED is instead directed to include Level II operational guidelines in the Ministry's programme.
implementation_status.note: Read from the enacted text as signed. The act establishes the hospital in law; whether it has been built and staffed is not recorded here.

citizen_questions.q: Is there now a hospital in Maimbung?
citizen_questions.a: In law, yes — the act establishes a Level II district hospital with 100-bed capacity there. Whether it has been built and staffed depends on the annual budget, and the act sets no deadline.

The Integrated Provincial Health Office – Sulu holds direct administrative and technical supervision. The regional Ministry of Health sets the operational guidelines and receives the annual operational plan.

citizen_questions.q: Where does the money come from?
citizen_questions.a: Salaries and operating costs are to be included in the annual General Appropriations Act of the Bangsamoro. No amount is named in the act.
Yes, but any increase in bed capacity or upgrading of services must be based on the annual hospital development plan prepared with IPHO-Sulu.
